races.paceDynamic: Minella Supreme, Hitak, Kamino Bello and Claude will ensure a strong gallop from the outset, with the former trio particularly keen early leaders who rarely settle. With 28 runners and multiple confirmed front-runners, this will be run at a searching pace that will test stamina reserves over the extended 2m3½f trip. The relentless tempo will suit hold-up horses like Radiator Springs, Aguellid and Sir Allen who can pick up the pieces, while prominent racers may struggle to sustain their position. This pace scenario strongly favours patient hold-up performers who can deliver late kicks.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If the multiple front-runners engage in a speed duel through the middle stages
scenarios.body: The searching gallop will find out the stamina-light runners, setting up a finish dominated by closers who have conserved energy. Hold-up horses with proven staying power will sweep past tired leaders in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tactical Battle
scenarios.trigger: If the pace leaders show restraint and settle into a more measured rhythm
scenarios.body: The race becomes more tactical with prominent racers able to maintain their positions, creating a more conventional finish where class and current form prevail. Those with tactical speed from mid-pack positions will be ideally placed.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one of the pace-setters gets an uncontested lead and kicks clear turning in
scenarios.body: A single front-runner breaks free from the pack while the others battle behind, maintaining enough of a margin to hold off late challengers. Early positioning becomes crucial with those tracking the leader best placed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Stamina Test Grind
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong throughout but no horse can quicken decisively
scenarios.body: The race becomes a test of pure stamina where the most battle-hardened stayers prevail through sheer determination rather than tactical positioning. Those with proven form at longer distances will outlast classier but less robust rivals.

watchPoints.text: Minella Supreme and Hitak could set unsustainable fractions if they lead together, creating a pace collapse

Multiple runners returning from long absences including Falcon Eight (430d) and Minella Post (450d) face fitness questions
Katie Daniels showed dramatic improvement in tongue-tie last time and retains the headgear for this assignment

races.paceDynamic: L'Evangeliste, Raise You Up, and Dunleer Crystal will force a strong early gallop over this stamina-sapping 2m3½f trip on yielding ground. With 6 horses wanting prominent positions (Los Blanco, Grey Jude, Green Angel, Vitorio Piel, Ifallgoeswell, Simply Natural), congestion is inevitable approaching the business end. The relentless pace combined with the testing conditions will stretch the field and expose stamina limitations. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can stay out of trouble early and finish with one sustained run when the pace collapses.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners maintain their aggressive gallop through halfway
scenarios.body: The strong early pace will take its toll on yielding ground, setting up perfectly for closers who avoided the early traffic. Eagle's Quest and All Night Revival can time their runs to perfection as the prominent brigade weakens.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one of the well-positioned runners can avoid the early traffic jam
scenarios.body: Simply Natural or Vitorio Piel could find a clear path and have enough left to resist late challengers after getting first run on the leaders. Their class ratings suggest they can handle the pace better than most.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If L'Evangeliste or Raise You Up can dictate terms without serious pressure
scenarios.body: The leader could steal enough of a march to hold off challengers, particularly if the prominent horses get involved in scrimmaging behind. L'Evangeliste's Galway win suggests he can make all when allowed to.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Maiden Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is even stronger than expected and ruins the fancied runners
scenarios.body: The extreme gallop could level the playing field, allowing a lightly-raced improver like The First Turn to capitalise on superior fitness. Chaos in the betting favourites opens the door for outsiders.

L'Evangeliste returning after 151 days off may need the run despite his obvious class advantage
Eagle's Quest switching back from Flat runs could be sharper than ratings suggest
Dunleer Crystal's front-running style puts him on collision course with two other confirmed leaders
The First Turn represents yard having first runner, debut market support would be significant

races.paceDynamic: Soir De Garde and Le Grand Peinture will contest the early pace from the front, with Soir De Garde having shown good tactical speed at Tramore and Le Grand Peinture proven to make all when winning at Navan. Behind them, Riskaway, Begorra Man, Mister Pessimistic and Quinta Do Lago will all want prominent positions, creating significant congestion turning for home. The five hold-up horses (Bunting, Milan Forth, Tinto De Verano, Minella Boss) will need gaps in what could become a messy finish. This pace setup strongly favours the prominent runners who can secure good position early and avoid the inevitable traffic problems.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace Benefits Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If Soir De Garde and Le Grand Peinture go hard early and string out the field
scenarios.body: The honest gallop will expose the weaker horses and give the front two a tactical advantage over the hold-up brigade. Soir De Garde has Paul Townend's tactical nous while Le Grand Peinture made all when winning for this yard.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Traffic Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the five prominent runners get bottled up behind the leaders turning in
scenarios.body: The congestion will create a cavalry charge finish where the strongest stayer from the prominent group prevails. Riskaway and Begorra Man have shown they handle scrimmaging while Quinta Do Lago lacks the experience.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Clear Run
scenarios.trigger: If Bunting or Minella Boss find a clear passage up the inner or outer
scenarios.body: The class of Bunting (OR 134) or recent winner Minella Boss could prove superior with racing room. Both need luck but have the ability to capitalize if the pace collapses.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Slow Early Messy Finish
scenarios.trigger: If both leaders go too slow and the field arrives en masse
scenarios.body: A bunched finish where any of the top six could win in a sprint. The 5lb claimer on Le Grand Peinture or 7lb claimer on Milan Forth might prove decisive in a tight finish.

watchPoints.text: Riskaway and Begorra Man could clash for the same prominent position behind the leaders
Bunting needs significant pace collapse to be competitive given his hold-up style
Quinta Do Lago's inexperience could tell if caught in traffic turning for home
Le Grand Peinture's 66-day absence after being pulled up raises fitness concerns
Mister Pessimistic faces big step up from maiden company after long layoff

races.name: Channor Real Estate Group Novice Hurdle (Grade 1)

runners_data.name: Le Frimeur
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with solid recent form but faces significant step up in class from maiden company
runners_data.comment: 2-2 over hurdles; big step up in grade but respected
runners_data.spotlight: Won Nenagh maiden point-to-point last season and 2-2 over hurdles this campaign, in 2m4f Chepstow maiden (soft) and keen enough and novicey in jumping in 2m5f Newbury novices' last month (good-to-soft); big step up in grade but respected.

runners_data.name: Dream On Mick
runners_data.note: Prominent style but trainer's poor 14-day record (0/12) raises immediate concerns about readiness
runners_data.comment: Carlisle winner the type to relish 3m but this a huge jump in class
runners_data.spotlight: Bought for £42,000 in January after winning a Tinahely maiden point-to-point (soft) and successful debut for connections in 2m4f Carlisle maiden hurdle early this month, clear with a hot favourite going to the last (good-to-soft); type to relish 3m but this a huge jump in class.

runners_data.name: Kazansky
runners_data.note: Strong on heavy ground but question marks over this softer surface and 47 days since last run
runners_data.comment: Didn't really land a blow (pulled up) in Albert Bartlett on latest and others preferred
runners_data.spotlight: Nicely progressive on heavy ground over the winter, winning Limerick Grade 2 novice and chased home 8l winner Doctor Steinberg over 2m6f at the DRF at Leopardstown; didn't really land a blow (pulled up) in 3m Albert Bartlett on latest and others now preferred.

runners_data.name: The Passing Wife
runners_data.note: Proven at the trip with excellent Albert Bartlett form, suits prominent position in strong pace
runners_data.comment: Denied second by Fruit De Mer in Albert Bartlett; easier finish could suit
runners_data.spotlight: Steadily progressive since upped in trip, winning 2m3f maiden here before considerably better form in 3m Albert Bartlett last month, only conceding second late on to Fruit De Mer having led at the last; handles this better ground and easier finish could suit.

runners_data.name: Love Me Tender
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with three wins from six starts but yet to prove stamina beyond 2m3f
runners_data.comment: Leopardstown third to Doctor Steinberg gives him place claims at best
runners_data.spotlight: Won a bumper, maiden hurdle (2m3f) and 2m Grade 3 novice without being extended, all on good-to-yielding; acquitted himself creditably in Grade 1 Leopardstown novices', including third to stablemate Doctor Steinberg (2m6f, heavy); most recently not at same level back in trip in Grade 2 at Fairyhouse; place claims at best.

runners_data.name: Fruit De Mer
runners_data.note: Keen prominent runner whose enthusiasm could prove costly in this strongly-run contest
runners_data.comment: Albert Bartlett second may need to improve again to take this but quite possible
runners_data.spotlight: Point-to-point winner landed odds on hurdles debut in 2m3f Naas maiden and has contested Grade 1 novices' since, plenty keen when third over 2m4f at same venue and much better form in 22-runner 3m Albert Bartlett, travelling much better and would have gone very close but for hanging left run-in when beaten 1.5l (soft); that probably wasn't the strongest renewal but improving 6yo has to be considered a major player here.

runners_data.name: Frankie John
runners_data.note: Solid prominent performer but remote in recent Grade 1s and may lack the pace for this company
runners_data.comment: Aintree fourth a career-best but probably a stronger race so more needed
runners_data.spotlight: Leopardstown maiden winner has contested Grade 1 novices all three starts since, notably remote fifth to Doctor Steinberg at same venue and better form on latest at Aintree in 3m1f Sefton Novices' when decent fourth in first-time cheekpieces (good-to-soft); this probably a stronger race so more needed.

runners_data.name: Doctor Steinberg
runners_data.note: Headgear applied suggests connections seeking improvement from this classy front-rank performer
runners_data.comment: Albert Bartlett flop has to settle better and now hooded; quicker ground to contend with
runners_data.spotlight: Bumper winner has taken really well to hurdling, winning first three starts over a trip, notably Grade 2 Navan novice and Grade 1 Leopardstown contest (2m6f) at the DRF (beating Kazansky 8l) on heavy; much too keen and ultimately pulled up when favourite for Grade 1 Albert Bartlett on latest and hood now fitted; encounters much better ground now.

runners_data.name: Spinningayarn
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner who showed stamina limitations when third in Albert Bartlett last time
runners_data.comment: Albert Bartlett fifth has ground to make up on both Fruit De Mer and The Passing Wife
runners_data.spotlight: Point/bumper winner; won easily under no-nonsense rides from the front at Fairyhouse (2m4f, yielding) and here (2m3f, heavy) but met his match over 3m in Albert Bartlett when fifth (Fruit De Mer second, The Passing Wife third); clearly needs to find more.

runners_data.name: Generous Risk
runners_data.note: Prominent runner carrying mare's allowance but faces significant step up in grade
runners_data.comment: No disgrace in chasing home a top-class novice at Fairyhouse (2m4f)  but more needed
runners_data.spotlight: Won point-to-point for Donnchadh Doyle last March before selling for £250,000; placed in three bumpers before successful hurdles debut in 2m5f Leopardstown maiden last month, making most and going clear from last (soft); no disgrace in chasing home a top-class novice at Fairyhouse (2m4f) last time, but more needed.

runners_data.name: I Started A Joke
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist perfectly suited to strong pace, proven headgear wearer with solid recent form
runners_data.comment: Did well considering saddle slipped at Fairyhouse; 3m could bring more
runners_data.spotlight: Won 2m maiden here in January (soft-to-heavy) and excellent run following month when favourite in very competitive 19-runner 2m Leopardstown handicap, going clear with winner from last; took another step forward when third to a top-class novice in 2m4f Grade 2 Fairyhouse novice on latest (Generous Risk second) in first-time cheekpieces, despite slipped saddle; good chance he'll improve again at 3m and don't rule out.

runners_data.name: Hipop De Loire
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose Flat stamina could prove crucial, but pulled up twice recently over hurdles
runners_data.comment: Talented Flat performer but yet to convince over hurdles
runners_data.spotlight: Classy sort on the Flat, third in last year's Doncaster Cup; 9yo has had just four runs over hurdles, winning Galway maiden last summer, but pulled up on both starts since last month's return, never featuring in Albert Bartlett and again in Grade 2 Fairyhouse novice (Generous Risk second); cheekpieces tried last time persisted with.

runners_data.name: Zanoosh
runners_data.note: In-form mare seeking six-timer with topweight concession, prominent style suits tactical battle
runners_data.comment: Seeking a six-timer and longer trip could bring more improvement; sex allowance crucial
runners_data.spotlight: Rapidly improving mare is seeking a six-timer, notable wins being 2m7f Grade 3 Limerick mares' novice and early this month in 2m4f Fairyhouse Grade 1 mares' novice, leading last; all wins have been on soft/heavy but gives the impression she'll handle this better ground and could have more to offer at this longer trip.

runners_data.name: Espresso Milan
runners_data.note: Front-runner who may struggle to dominate against stronger pace-setting rivals
runners_data.comment: Didn't seem to get home in Albert Bartlett but worth this second chance at the trip
runners_data.spotlight: Beaten in three bumpers for Fergal O'Brien but successful on opening two hurdle runs for Willie Mullins, in 2m maiden here and ready winner of 2m6f Thurles novice (yielding); didn't seem to get home in 3m Albert Bartlett, but worth this second chance at the trip and remains a potential improver.

races.paceDynamic: Spinningayarn, Love Me Tender, and Espresso Milan will ensure a strong gallop from the start, with all three proven front-runners likely to jostle for the lead early. The genuine pace will stretch the field over 3m, creating gaps and testing stamina reserves in the final mile. Six runners wanting prominent positions (including Doctor Steinberg, Kazansky, and The Passing Wife) will create congestion and traffic problems from the third-last hurdle. This strong pace and tactical pressure heavily favors hold-up horses with proven finishing kicks who can avoid the early scrimmaging.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Benefits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners maintain a genuine gallop throughout
scenarios.body: The strong pace will stretch the field and set up perfectly for the two hold-up horses to deliver late challenges. I Started A Joke and Hipop De Loire can avoid early trouble and benefit from the stamina test.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If one of the high-class prominent runners can secure a clean passage
scenarios.body: Doctor Steinberg or The Passing Wife can track the pace without getting caught in traffic and have the class to quicken when it matters. Their proven Grade 1 form gives them the edge in a grueling finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Wires Field
scenarios.trigger: If Spinningayarn or Love Me Tender get an easy lead and controlled fractions
scenarios.body: The leader can dictate terms and prove hard to peg back over this stamina-sapping trip. Their front-running style is perfectly suited to Punchestown's long straight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners go off too fast and tie up badly
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish favoring horses with turn of foot rather than stamina. This scenario would suit the more versatile prominent runners who can quicken late.

watchPoints.text: Spinningayarn and Love Me Tender must be monitored early as both may over-race if disputing the lead together
The prominent brigade of Kazansky, Doctor Steinberg and The Passing Wife could create a traffic jam approaching the third-last hurdle
I Started A Joke needs Ryan's Gap and the back straight to be run at genuine pace to set up his finishing kick
Hipop De Loire's jumping must be watched closely given his two recent pull-ups over hurdles
Zanoosh faces her biggest test yet in this grade and the 7lb weight advantage may not be enough against these rivals

races.name: Race & Stay At Punchestown Champion I.N.H. Flat Race (Grade 1)

runners_data.name: Barnahash Prince
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse perfectly suited to strong early pace with stamina-laden pedigree and 24 days freshness advantage
runners_data.comment: Made a winning debut at Cork early in the month, faces a big step up in class now
runners_data.spotlight: Half-brother to bumper/2m4f hurdle winner Barnahash Primrose; dam bumper/2m6f Grade 3 hurdle winner; looked like a horse with a future over jumps when making a winning debut at Cork early in the month; faces a big step up in class now

runners_data.name: The Mourne Rambler
runners_data.note: Class hold-up performer with Noel Meade's 49-day preparation and two impressive wins on similar going
runners_data.comment: Sets a high standard with a handsome Cheltenham win, six of these rivals behind him then
runners_data.spotlight: Promising debut when second in a point at Portrush last October; made a good impression when landing a traditionally strong bumper at Leopardstown in December; thoroughly lived up to expectations when becoming the tenth consecutive Irish-trained winner of the Champion Bumper, staying on strongly after leading under Colin Keane a furlong down; sets the standard.

runners_data.name: Boycetown
runners_data.note: Front runner with tongue-tie fitted who must avoid getting drawn into early speed battle with five other pace-setters
runners_data.comment: Second-best of the Irish when fourth at Cheltenham; capable of making his presence felt
runners_data.spotlight: Bought for E120,000 after finishing second in a point; stepped up from C&D debut to record an emphatic win at Down Royal's Christmas meeting; had a tongue-tie added for the Grade 1 bumper at Cheltenham and reacted well to take fourth (second-best of the Irish) behind The Mourne Rambler; capable of making his presence felt.

runners_data.name: The Wager
runners_data.note: Mullins second-string with tactical pace but may get caught up in early gallop given forward-going style
runners_data.comment: Emerged from the Champion Bumper with more credit than several shorter-priced stablemates
runners_data.spotlight: Went close over C&D last season on his only start for Pat Doyle; battled well for a narrow success at Fairyhouse in January; emerged from the Champion Bumper with more credit than several shorter-priced stablemates; stayed on from an unpromising position to finish seventh, only a neck behind Quiryn, who was best of the Mullins squad.

runners_data.name: Dromard
runners_data.note: Lone-win newcomer for Mullins with stamina-rich pedigree but 53 days off track raises fitness questions
runners_data.comment: Impressed on heavy going on debut. Patrick Mullins picks him ahead of Cheltenham also-rans
runners_data.spotlight: Dam French hurdle/chase winner, half-sister to Prix du Cadran winner and Ascot Gold Cup third, Le Miracle; runaway winner of a heavy-ground Gowran bumper on debut on the eve of the Cheltenham Festival; would not have been out of place in that event if he had made it to the track earlier; gets a vote of confidence from Patrick Mullins.

runners_data.name: The Irish Avatar
runners_data.note: Front runner stepping up significantly in class after easy Fairyhouse win but lacks experience at this level
runners_data.comment: Only fourth-best for the stable in an untypically tame challenge at Cheltenham
runners_data.spotlight: Changed hands for £200,000 after finishing second in a point for Colin Bowe last April; reappeared in January for an all-the-way 9l victory on soft-to-heavy at Navan, form franked by the runner-up Low Kick in winning by 10l at Naas; only fourth-best for the stable in an untypically tame challenge at Cheltenham; probably capable of much better.

runners_data.name: With Nolimit
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who showed improved form when second in Grade 2, suits tactical scenarios better than strong pace
runners_data.comment: Grade 2 runner-up after Fairyhouse win, ninth behind The Mourne Rambler at Cheltenham
runners_data.spotlight: Point winner last season, won five-runner Fairyhouse bumper in January; finished well when narrowly failing to reel in stablemate Broadway Ted in a Grade 2 at Leopardstown; finished in mid-division at Cheltenham.

runners_data.name: Love Sign d'Aunou
runners_data.note: Front runner with 24-length debut win but completely unexposed at this level of competition
runners_data.comment: Impressed on debut, better ground found him out at Cheltenham, rejected by Patrick Mullins
runners_data.spotlight: Point winner for Ger Quinn at Loughanmore a year ago; bolted up by 24l from dual points winner Largy Star on heavy ground at Naas in January on debut for Willie Mullins; sent off joint-favourite at Cheltenham, failed to cope with ground officially described as good, and dropped away to finish 17l behind The Mourne Rambler.

runners_data.name: Low Kick
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with 66 days off track but classy profile and ideal tactical position for expected pace scenario
runners_data.comment: Stepped up from debut behind The Irish Avatar with 10l Naas win; seems ground-versatile
runners_data.spotlight: Showed promise when third in a 17-runner bumper at Aintree last May for Jack Teal; bought for £170,000 at Goffs UK sale five days later; reappeared at Navan in January, chasing home odds-on winner The Irish Avatar (same ownership); showed the benefit of the run when a 10l winner at Naas in February; seems ground-versatile.

runners_data.name: Of Land And Sea
runners_data.note: Front runner with headgear changes but outclassed on ratings and Cheltenham saddle slip raises reliability concerns
runners_data.comment: Enterprisingly ridden very wide to win at Limerick, saddle slipped at Cheltenham
runners_data.spotlight: Huge price at Cheltenham, lost all chance when the saddle slipped early; ridden by Patrick Mullins on all three Irish starts; enterprisingly-ridden very wide to win at Limerick.

races.paceDynamic: Boycetown, The Wager, Dromard, The Irish Avatar, Love Sign d'Aunou and Of Land And Sea will all want to be handy early, creating a fierce gallop from the start. With six confirmed front runners in a 10-horse field, the pace will be relentless and stamina-sapping over this testing 2m½f trip on yielding ground. The strong early gallop will stretch the field and set up a tactical finish where those who conserve energy early can strike late. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses and those with proven stamina reserves who can benefit from the inevitable pace collapse.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If the six front runners go too fast early and weaken significantly in the final half-mile
scenarios.body: The relentless gallop will set up perfectly for the three hold-up horses who can time their runs to perfection as the leaders tire. Barnahash Prince, The Mourne Rambler and Low Kick are ideally positioned to exploit the pace scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tactical Battle
scenarios.trigger: If the front runners moderate the pace slightly and several survive to fight out the finish
scenarios.body: A more measured gallop allows some pace-setters to retain enough energy for a sustained battle, but still favours those with tactical speed. The Mullins duo of The Wager and Love Sign d'Aunou have the class to dictate terms.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one pace-setter gets an uncontested lead while others fall away early
scenarios.body: Dromard or Boycetown could steal a march if the other front runners cancel each other out in the early exchanges. The winner would need exceptional stamina to resist the late closers on this testing ground.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Compromise Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is moderate but quickens dramatically late creating a sprint finish
scenarios.body: An unexpectedly tactical affair would suit those with the best turn of foot, though this seems unlikely given the number of confirmed front runners. With Nolimit's prominent style could be ideal in this scenario.

watchPoints.text: If Boycetown and Love Sign d'Aunou both go forward aggressively early, they could set suicidal fractions that rule both out
The Mourne Rambler needs a strong pace to be effective so watch if the front runners surprisingly go steady early
Dromard's 53-day layoff combined with debut run fitness questions make him vulnerable despite Mullins support
With Nolimit could be caught in no-man's land if positioned prominently when the pace turns into a sprint
Low Kick's 66-day break means his fitness must be taken on trust despite Gordon Elliott's preparation skills

races.name: Colm Quinn BMW Handicap Chase (Grade 3)

runners_data.name: Dee Capo
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits but heavy traffic likely with Kennedy aboard; 27 days fresh and course winner
runners_data.comment: 6lb higher than when winning here in November; more needed
runners_data.spotlight: Two chase wins including 2m6f handicap here in November (off 142) and at least as good form when staying-on fourth over same trip at the DRF; no match for stablemate Maxxum over 2m4f at Clonmel on latest; Jack Kennedy's pick.

runners_data.name: Classic Getaway
runners_data.note: Prominent style ideal for this but aging legs at 10; Mullins 6/30 in 14 days concerning
runners_data.comment: 3m too far last time, back to probably his optimum trip here so considered
runners_data.spotlight: Grade 2 Red Mills Chase winner at Gowran last season hasn't recaptured that level of form this term, although third in same event was a solid run; last of three in 3m Grade 3 Cork conditions event on latest, back to probably his optimum trip here so considered.

runners_data.name: Jesse Evans
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 206-day break; excellent going record but rust factor

runners_data.name: Conyers Hill
runners_data.note: Hold-up style disadvantaged by race shape; best recent form and Flanagan tactical
runners_data.comment: Didn't stay 3m1f in Thyestes; has had time off since, could go well back to optimum trip
runners_data.spotlight: Novice win came at Down Royal last season and pick of this season's handicap form when fourth in 2m4f Paddy Power Gold Cup at Cheltenham and held narrow lead when faller two out in 2m4f Tim Duggan Memorial at Limerick over Christmas; didn't stay 3m1f in Thyestes following month and has had time off since; could go well.

runners_data.name: Down Memory Lane
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner faces traffic nightmare; Walsh aboard but 23 days since last run

runners_data.name: Riaan
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits perfectly; 210-day absence major concern despite beating Jesse Evans last time
runners_data.comment: Sligo winner has run well fresh and has his ground here so one to consider
runners_data.spotlight: Chase wins have been at Wexford and Sligo on decent ground, latter occasion when beating Jesse Evans 3.5l at levels in October when last seen, albeit steady pace possibly suited; has run well fresh and has his ground here, so one to consider.

runners_data.name: King Alexander
runners_data.note: Hold-up type but Townend's tactical brilliance; lightly-raced novice with upside
runners_data.comment: Cheltenham handicap debut fourth augurs well; ground fine
runners_data.spotlight: Lightly-raced novice landed odds in 2m4f Gowran beginners' in February and fine effort for one so inexperienced when fourth of 18 in 2m5f Jack Richards Novices' Handicap at Cheltenham on much better ground; more scope for improvement than most of these.

runners_data.name: Dreal Deal
runners_data.note: Hold-up veteran at 11; best recent form but style wrong for this race shape
runners_data.comment: Haydock veterans handicap third promising; whether or not he can back that up debatable
runners_data.spotlight: Last win came at Killarney last summer but retains level of ability judged on recent Haydock veterans' handicap third (good), best run for some time; whether or not he can back that up against more progressive types is debatable.

runners_data.name: Karia Des Blaises
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with Cobden visiting; Listed winner but traffic concerns remain
runners_data.comment: Ran no sort of race in Irish National but not to be ruled out off a fair mark here
runners_data.spotlight: French hurdle winner; useful form in defeat over fences last season, off the mark when running away with 2m6f Thurles Listed mares' novice in February (soft-to-heavy); ran no sort of race in 3m5f Irish National latest, but not to be ruled out off a fair mark here.

runners_data.name: Where's My Jet
runners_data.note: Perfect front-running position as sole leader; 0-7 over fences but race setup ideal
runners_data.comment: Penultimate Leopardstown run was decent but others preferred
runners_data.spotlight: Hurdles winner is 0-7 chasing, decent run in very valuable 2m6f Leopardstown Handicap at the DRF (soft) but never counted following month in Jack Richards Novices' Handicap at Cheltenham; others look more reliable.

runners_data.name: Kilbarry Saint
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits; 5lb claiming jockey O'Brien and trainer with 0/1 record

runners_data.name: Nouvotic
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 185-day break; strong course record but absence worry
runners_data.comment: Absent since Wexford win in October off 122; conditions to suit and likely more to offer
runners_data.spotlight: Lightly raced but already a better chaser than hurdler, two wins coming over 2m4f at Wexford, most recently showing good attitude back in October on good-to-yielding; absent since but conditions to suit and likely more to offer.

runners_data.name: Midnight It Is
runners_data.note: Hold-up sprinter likely needs shorter trip; 50 days off and wrong race shape
runners_data.comment: Didn't seem to get home in 2m4f Plate last month; stamina concerns remain at this trip
runners_data.spotlight: Hurdle winner at 2m3f but rarely ventures beyond 2m1f now, good third in last season's Grand Annual at Cheltenham but didn't seem to get home in 2m4f Plate at same venue last month; stamina concerns remain at this trip.

runners_data.name: Magic McColgan
runners_data.note: Prominent maiden chaser; 0-5 this term but recent form suggests improvement
runners_data.comment: Never travelled latest, previous Naas second would give her definite claims
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden hurdle winner here last season (2m4f, soft) is 0-5 chasing this term, standout run when only caught close home by a strong favourite in 2m4f Naas handicap in February (heavy), having hit the last; reportedly never travelled before pulled up over 3m at Navan last month, but claims if back to her Naas form.

races.paceDynamic: Where's My Jet is the sole confirmed front runner and will set his own tempo without pressure in the early stages. Six horses want prominent positions (Classic Getaway, Jesse Evans, Riaan, Kilbarry Saint, Nouvotic, Magic McColgan) creating significant congestion behind the leader from halfway onwards. The large field of hold-up horses (Dee Capo, Conyers Hill, Down Memory Lane, King Alexander, Dreal Deal, Karia Des Blaises, Midnight It Is) will be squeezed for racing room as the prominent pack compresses approaching two out. This race shape strongly favours front-running and early prominent tactics, as the traffic jam building behind will compromise late closers.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Where's My Jet gets an easy lead and maintains jumping rhythm...
scenarios.body: The lone pace-setter builds an unassailable advantage while the prominent brigade battle amongst themselves behind. Hold-up horses face an impossible task recovering lost ground through heavy traffic.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Traffic Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the six prominent runners bunch up and create interference 2-3 out...
scenarios.body: Kilbarry Saint or Nouvotic benefit from better positioning within the prominent pack while hold-up horses are trapped. The early leader gets caught by whoever navigates the congestion best.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Hero Finds Gap
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and clear splits appear approaching the last...
scenarios.body: One of the class hold-up horses (Dee Capo or King Alexander) threads through late with Kennedy or Townend's tactical nous proving decisive. The front division comes back to the field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Mid-Race Tempo Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Jesse Evans or Classic Getaway press Where's My Jet from early in back straight...
scenarios.body: A genuine pace battle develops between the front three, setting up the race for a staying type who can quicken off the strong gallop. Late closers benefit from the increased tempo.

watchPoints.text: Where's My Jet's jumping under pressure - if he makes an error when challenged his 0-7 chase record suggests capitulation
Traffic buildup behind leaders from 2 out - Jesse Evans and Classic Getaway most likely to cause interference
Kennedy's route-finding on Dee Capo - champion jockey's tactical decisions crucial in heavy traffic
Jesse Evans and Nouvotic both returning from long absences - watch for early signs of ring-rustiness
Riaan's fitness after 210 days off - previously beat Jesse Evans but massive gap since last run

races.name: Ladbrokes Punchestown Gold Cup (Chase) (Grade 1)

runners_data.name: Gaelic Warrior
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with 47 days freshening up, top-rated on 176 and Paul Townend's tactical nous crucial over this staying trip
runners_data.comment: Impressive Cheltenham Gold Cup winner, has a stronger Punchestown record than Fact To File
runners_data.spotlight: Confirmed his staying power with Bowl win at Aintree last year; got his campaign off to a fine start with John Durkan victory from Fact To File over 2m4f here; third in a blanket finish in the King George before 5l second to a restored Fact To File at Leopardstown; travelled powerfully for stunningly impressive Gold Cup triumph to leap-frog Fact To File in the ratings.

runners_data.name: Fact To File
runners_data.note: Natural leader who'll want to dictate from the front, 86 days since last run could be perfect prep for this Grade 1 assignment
runners_data.comment: Avenged John Durkan loss when beating Gaelic Warrior at Leopardstown, intriguing rematch
runners_data.spotlight: 2024 Brown Advisory winner, 2025 Ryanair winner; won the 2024 John Durkan at this venue, had a hard race when narrowly beaten by Gaelic Warrior in this season's repeat bid; failed to do himself justice in the King George; back to best when readily beating Gaelic Warrior and Galopin Des Champs in the Irish Gold Cup; fascinating rematch now after bypassing Ryanair.

runners_data.name: Champ Kiely
runners_data.note: Front-runner having a torrid season but dropped back to 3m+ suits, needs to avoid early speed duel with Fact To File
runners_data.comment: Won the Grade 1 novice here last year, making up the numbers on this season's evidence
runners_data.spotlight: Won the Grade 1 novice here last year, beating stablemate Ballyburn; has experienced a torrid campaign after starting off with a second placing over 2m; remote seventh behind Fact To File in the Irish Gold Cup; not a bad effort in the Grand National; making up the numbers here.

runners_data.name: Inothewayurthinkin
runners_data.note: Hold-up merchant requiring significant form turnaround, but Gavin Cromwell knows how to peak this horse for big targets
runners_data.comment: 2025 Cheltenham Gold Cup hero, looks safely held by Gaelic Warrior on last month's clash
runners_data.spotlight: Cheltenham Gold Cup winner last year; no sign of best form on his first three runs this term; repeated previous Cheltenham trend of leaving winter form behind to finish third in the Gold Cup, despite not jumping particularly well; 0-4 at this venue and was trounced by Gaelic Warrior here as a novice; will need to catch the big two on an off-day.

runners_data.name: Grangeclare West
runners_data.note: Another hold-up runner who benefits from strong pace, 18-day turnaround suggests Willie Mullins has him primed
runners_data.comment: Third in the 2025 Grand National, exited at the first this year, stable's third string now
runners_data.spotlight: Excellent third in last season's Grand National; set tough tasks in Grade 1s this season before dropped in class to beat Gerri Colombe in the Bobbyjo at Fairyhouse; unseated at the first when 9-1 for the Grand National; stable's third string now.

races.paceDynamic: Fact To File and Champ Kiely will contest the early lead, establishing a genuine gallop over this extended trip at Punchestown. With both natural front-runners committed to racing prominently, they'll create an honest tempo that stretches through the first two miles. The hold-up horses Gaelic Warrior, Inothewayurthinkin and Grangeclare West will track this pace from mid-division before launching their challenges from the back of the last fence. This strong early gallop favours the hold-up merchants who can use their finishing kick when the pace-setters tire.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Fact To File and Champ Kiely duel too hard early and compromise each other
scenarios.body: The honest pace will perfectly set up the race for the closers who can time their runs to perfection. Gaelic Warrior's class and Inothewayurthinkin's Gold Cup winning ability make them prime beneficiaries of this likely scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If Fact To File gets an uncontested lead with Champ Kiely settling just behind
scenarios.body: The 2025 Ryanair winner can dictate terms and kick clear before the hold-up horses get into gear. His proven stamina at this trip gives him the edge over Champ Kiely in a front-running battle.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Class Tells Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses early and becomes a sprint from the last
scenarios.body: Gaelic Warrior's superior class rating of 176 and Paul Townend's timing become decisive factors. The John Durkan winner can overcome any tactical scenario when the race becomes about pure ability rather than pace dynamics.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Cromwell Surprise Package
scenarios.trigger: If Inothewayurthinkin rediscovers his Cheltenham Gold Cup form at the right moment
scenarios.body: The defending Gold Cup winner's fresh approach under Keith Donoghue could catch the Mullins-trained favourites napping. His hold-up style perfectly suits any pace scenario but requires a significant improvement on recent form.

watchPoints.text: Fact To File and Champ Kiely could destroy each other's chances if they engage in a prolonged speed duel from flagfall
Gaelic Warrior needs Paul Townend to position him perfectly in the small field to time his challenge from the back of the last
Inothewayurthinkin's early positioning will reveal Keith Donoghue's confidence levels in his mount's current form
Grangeclare West could be the forgotten horse if the market focuses entirely on the Gaelic Warrior-Fact To File clash
The small five-runner field means any early faller or refusal dramatically changes the tactical dynamic for the survivors

races.name: Weatherbys General Stud Book Irish EBF Mares INH Flat Race (Grade 3)

runners_data.name: Maximillian Lady
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with proven stamina who excels when races become tactical battles, 208 days off a concern
runners_data.comment: Galway winner returns from 9 months' absence for new yard with hood fitted
runners_data.spotlight: Useful level of form earlier in the season for Cormac Farrell, running away with Galway mares' event (good-to-yielding) and clear second to an odds-on shot in Gowran mares' Listed contest (soft); returns from 9 months' absence for new yard with hood fitted.

runners_data.name: Treadonmydreams
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with limited experience, beaten 18 lengths by Kiltybo last time so faces massive task
runners_data.comment: Beaten 18l behind Kiltybo on bumper debut at Naas so lots to find; tongue-tie fitted
runners_data.spotlight: Dead-heated in a point in 2024, her sole start in that sphere; beaten 18l behind Kiltybo on bumper debut at Naas last month so lots to find; tongue-tie fitted.

runners_data.name: Even Tho
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with tactical speed, bounced back well from fall to win last time for in-form Mullins yard
runners_data.comment: Decisive Limerick success; could well play a role if handling quicker conditions
runners_data.spotlight: Half-sister to useful bumper and 2m4f-2m5f hurdle/chase winner The Enabler; fell when having the race at her mercy in Dromahane point-to-point in December and debuted for champion trainer with decisive Limerick bumper success last month (first two well clear); nice prospect who could well play a role if handling quicker conditions.

runners_data.name: Goulmichette
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced with unknown best trip, turned over as odds-on favourite last time which raises questions
runners_data.comment: Too keen at Ayr, given a break since and hood now fitted
runners_data.spotlight: Ran away with Quakerstown point-to-point last season before fetching 170,000euros at this meeting; reappeared when turned over at long-odds on in Ayr mares' bumper in February, not getting home after pulling herself into clear early lead (third to now stablemate Latosca Du Houx); given a break since and hood now fitted.

runners_data.name: Sapphire Jewel
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who was keen on debut, gets weight allowance but lacks experience for this level
runners_data.comment: Remote third to Even Tho on Limerick debut; hard to see her reversing that form
runners_data.spotlight: Sister to bumper winner and decent 2m4f novice hurdle winner Frankie John; plenty keen on last month's debut when a remote third to Even Tho at Limerick; has ability but hard to see her reversing that form.

runners_data.name: Born Believing
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with perfect recent record, tongue-tie applied suggests connections expect improvement
runners_data.comment: Got up close home at Cork; staying type will appreciate a truly-run race
runners_data.spotlight: Sister to useful 2m3f-3m4f hurdle/chase winner Born Braver among others; won Belharbour mares' maiden point-to-point on debut in February and followed up early this month in Cork pointers' bumper, needing every yard to get up close home (yielding) to beat Tintara; will appreciate a truly-run race.

runners_data.name: Latosca Du Houx
runners_data.note: Natural leader who impressed when making all at Cork, half-sister to smart performers
runners_data.comment: Ayr winner for Nicky Richards has since joined top yard; respected
runners_data.spotlight: Half-sister to useful 2m/2m1f hurdle winner After Rain and French bumper winner Ultramaille; dam French 2m2f chase winner; had Goulmichette back in third when making winning Ayr debut in February for Nicky Richards, readily picking up that free-running rival a furlong out, despite looking green; has since joined top yard and interesting addition to its very strong challenge here.

runners_data.name: Belladaball
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner much improved last time, tongue-tie fitted and well-suited to tactical affairs
runners_data.comment: Came off strong pace for Fairyhouse win; quicker ground but definite player if handling it
runners_data.spotlight: Half-sister to bumper winner and smart hurdler/chaser Meetingofthewaters; some promise first two bumpers but much improved to land Fairyhouse mares' Listed event early this month, coming off strong pace to win going away from Wonderful Everyday and Some Pretender on yielding-to-soft; quicker ground here but definite player if handling it.

runners_data.name: Glens Anthem
runners_data.note: Front-runner from excellent staying family, made all on debut and bred to handle this trip
runners_data.comment: Impressed on recent Navan debut; Patrick Mullins stays loyal and likely major player
runners_data.spotlight: Harzand half-sister to bumper winners Shantou's Melody and Glens Lullaby; dam smart bumper (at this meeting) and 2m2f-2m6f hurdle winner, sister to bumper/2m hurdle winner Glens Harmony; created good impression on last month's Navan debut, patiently ridden and readily going away from favourite final furlong (soft); Patrick Mullins stays loyal and likely major player.

runners_data.name: Al Arrivee
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with Gold Cup bloodline, long absence since last run but has class on her day
runners_data.comment: Absent since Galway festival second last summer; top amateur rider booked
runners_data.spotlight: Half-sister to Cheltenham Gold Cup winner Al Boum Photo; runner-up on Galway debut last season and returned to win at Sligo last summer (good) before returning to Galway at the festival when finishing a clear second to the smart Murat; absent again since but clearly goes well fresh and top amateur rider booked.

runners_data.name: Tintara
runners_data.note: Leading type who has fallen in both point-to-points, sister to smart performers but unreliable
runners_data.comment: Outpointed late by Born Believing at Cork early this month; this a lot stiffer task
runners_data.spotlight: Half-sister to winners, notably Tombstone (smart bumper and 2m-2m3f hurdler/chaser) and Tintangle (useful bumper and 2m-2m2f hurdler/chaser); fell in her first two point-to-points; bought for 55,000GBP after a second-place finish in a mares' maiden at Ballycrystal and only outpointed close home by Born Believing on Cork bumper debut early this month; this looks a lot stiffer task.

runners_data.name: Wonderful Everyday
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who won this race last year, struggled on softer ground but back on suitable surface
runners_data.comment: Has 3l to find with Belladaball from Fairyhouse; better ground should suit
runners_data.spotlight: Did well to beat the geldings on debut in Goffs Defender Bumper at this meeting last year (yielding), but had run nowhere near that level on softer ground until much more encouraging effort at Fairyhouse early this month when staying-on second to Belladaball in mares' Listed contest (yielding-to-soft); same terms here so more needed, but better ground to suit.

runners_data.name: Some Pretender
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with solid recent form, consistent performer who handles all conditions
runners_data.comment: Third to Belladaball at Fairyhouse; hard to see her reversing that form on same terms
runners_data.spotlight: Had two subsequent winners behind when justifying favouritism at Galway on debut in August (2m1f, good) and solid runs in defeat in three outings since without really progressing, most recently making most when third to Belladaball (Wonderful Everyday second) in Fairyhouse mares' Listed contest early this month; looking exposed and hard to see her reversing that form on same terms.

runners_data.name: Coole Cafe
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist in excellent form, gets weight allowance and thrives under patient tactics
runners_data.comment: Quickened nicely for two wins; quicker ground could see her in an even better light
runners_data.spotlight: Surprise winner of Navan academy hurdle (soft) in December and improved markedly from bumper debut for wins at Naas and Limerick (Listed) under hold-up rides in testing conditions with hood fitted; has a tidy turn of foot and quicker ground could see her in an even better light.

runners_data.name: Kiltybo
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with forcing tactics, exposed but brings proven stamina for this trip
runners_data.comment: Front-running wins at Thurles and Naas; exposed at Aintree so more needed
runners_data.spotlight: Brings good bit of experience to the table, having won mares' bumpers at Thurles and Naas under forcing tactics; seemingly exposed under similar tactics at Aintree recently, but would be a dangerous one to give a soft lead to.

runners_data.name: Celestial Tune
runners_data.note: Leading type in good current form, tongue-tie applied and has won two Listed bumpers this season
runners_data.comment: Too keen at the DRF; claims on wins at Listowel and Cheltenham though
runners_data.spotlight: Half-sister to bumper winner Katie Connell; debut runner-up at this meeting last year and has returned this season to win mares' Listed bumpers at Listowel and Cheltenham, each time made plenty of use of; too keen and pulled up in Grade 2 mares' event at the DRF and has been given a break since; not out of it if settling.

races.paceDynamic: Kiltybo, Latosca Du Houx, Glens Anthem and Tintara will ensure a proper gallop from the outset, with Celestial Tune also likely to track close. This quartet of confirmed front-runners in a 16-runner field guarantees a searching pace that will test stamina reserves over this extended trip on yielding ground. The strong early gallop will stretch the field and create gaps, with the pace likely to soften mid-race before intensifying again from the two-furlong pole. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses and those who can produce sustained finishing kicks, as the early burn-up will set up a classic scenario for closers to sweep past tiring pace-setters.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace-setters go too hard early and tie up in the final furlong
scenarios.body: The strong gallop plays perfectly into the hands of Coole Cafe, Wonderful Everyday and Belladaball who can time their runs to perfection. These proven closers will have plenty to aim at as the front-runners weaken, with the yielding ground suiting their sustained finishing style.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Suits Prominents
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners go steady early before quickening from halfway
scenarios.body: Born Believing and Even Tho can position prominently without over-racing and have the class to respond when the pace lifts. These horses avoid the early burn-up while staying close enough to strike when the race develops in earnest.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Survives Pressure
scenarios.trigger: If one pace-setter gets first run and holds on gamely
scenarios.body: Latosca Du Houx or Glens Anthem could steal a march by dictating terms and having enough left to repel late challenges. The Mullins pair have the quality to sustain their effort when others come at them in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Stamina Test Favours Stayers
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly searching throughout and becomes a war of attrition
scenarios.body: Al Arrivee's Gold Cup bloodline and Maximillian Lady's proven stamina reserves could prove decisive in a grueling finish. These horses have the pedigree and experience to keep finding when others reach their limit.

watchPoints.text: Kiltybo and Latosca Du Houx could set suicidal fractions if they engage in an early speed duel
Coole Cafe's inexperience at this level could be exposed if the pace becomes stop-start rather than searching
Al Arrivee's 269-day absence makes her fitness a major question mark despite her obvious class
Even Tho's jumping background could prove an asset if the pace becomes messy and she needs to switch course
Born Believing's perfect recent record makes her dangerous if she can secure an ideal tracking position
